banner: Run FFmpeg and ffprobe on files in this browser workspace. Media processing stays on this device.
title: Make a six-second demo
subtitle: Choose a video, inspect its contents, then write a command to keep the useful part.

source.heading: Start with a recording
source.intro: Use the practice video, import a recording or record your screen. File setup uses the app controls below.
source.sampleNote: A twelve-second recording of Find and Replace in Mousepad, an independent text editor. The recording has no sound.
source.importNote: Choose a video from this device. A copy is saved in this browser workspace.
source.recordUnavailable: Screen recording is unavailable in this browser. Use the practice video or import a recording.
source.loaded: Practice video loaded. Replay it, then continue to Inspect.
source.importedReady: Video selected. Replay it, then continue to Inspect.
source.privacy: Files stay in this browser workspace on this device. Download important work: browser storage can be removed.
source.watch: Watch staging change to production in the configuration file. Check whether both replacements and the final text are readable.

source.playbackError: This browser could not play the file. Download it to try another player, or choose a different source.

inspect.heading: Find out what is in the file
inspect.intro: Run ffprobe with a filename to read its usual media summary without changing the file. A stream is a sequence of related media data, such as pictures or sound.
inspect.task: Find the Duration line and each Stream line. The practice recording has one video stream and no audio stream.
inspect.predict: The practice recording is silent. Do you expect ffprobe to list an audio stream?
inspect.resultNote: This report comes from the ffprobe command you ran against the selected workspace file.
inspect.importResult: ffprobe reports the contents of your imported file. Compare its streams and duration with what you meant to record.
inspect.streamSummary: The practice recording contains H.264 video and no audio stream. Its container duration is twelve seconds.
inspect.customResult: These are the results of your typed command. Read the output before continuing.

trim.heading: Keep the action and its result
trim.intro: For the practice video, start at two seconds and keep six seconds. Replay the edit to decide whether the action and result are clear.
trim.task: Choose a start time and duration. Read the command as it changes, run it, then replay the output.
trim.importTask: Replay your recording and choose a start time and duration that keep the useful action. Check the resulting edit before sharing it.
trim.predict: Change the duration from six seconds to four. Which part of the viewing time are you removing?
trim.resultNote: FFmpeg produced this file. Replay it to check the action, result and any intended sound.
trim.review: Can a viewer follow the action and read its result? Check sound only if you intended it.
trim.exportUnavailable: Run an FFmpeg command successfully to create a downloadable output.
trim.tryAgain: Change the command and try again
trim.sourceSafe: Choose a different output filename to keep the source.

command.heading: Your command
command.builderNote: Choose values beside the FFmpeg options. The complete command remains visible and can be copied or edited.
command.manualNote: Edit the command directly. Switching views keeps your draft.
command.nativeBoundary: These are FFmpeg and ffprobe commands. To use them in a terminal, install the tools and put the source file in your working folder.
command.browserBoundary: Commands use files in this browser workspace. Shell pipes, redirection and variable expansion are unavailable. ffprobe shows its usual media summary; add -of json and report options for structured output.
command.probeDefault: Run ffprobe on the source to read its usual media summary.
command.outputHint: Use a new .mp4 filename to keep the original.
command.copyFailed: Select the command text and copy it with your device's copy control.
command.downloadNote: The download contains the command text. Review it before running it on your computer.
command.empty: Enter an FFmpeg or ffprobe command first.
command.wrongTool: Use ffmpeg or ffprobe here. Loading files and replaying media use the app controls.
command.customWarning: You edited this command directly. Returning to the builder would replace it with the builder's current values.
command.typedRestored: Your typed command has been restored.
command.invalidTime: Use a start time of zero or more and a duration greater than zero.
command.invalidImport: Choose a nonempty video file no larger than 20 MiB.
command.rangeOutside: The practice video lasts twelve seconds. Choose a start time and duration whose total is no more than twelve seconds.
command.chooseReport: Select streams, container information or both before running the inspection.
command.invalidOutput: Choose a new filename ending in .mp4. Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens or underscores.
command.sameOutput: Choose a different output filename to keep your source.

flags.heading: Read the options
flags.input: -i names an input file. The final filename names the output.
flags.probeStreams: -show_streams reports each picture or sound stream.
flags.probeFormat: -show_format reports the container, which organises the streams and their timing.
flags.probeDefault: ffprobe FILE shows the usual Duration and Stream lines. Each Stream line describes pictures, sound or other media in the file. The original file is unchanged.
flags.probeJson: For a structured report, switch to Type command and add -show_streams -show_format -of json. You can also add -v error to hide routine log messages.
flags.start: Here, -ss comes after -i. FFmpeg decodes the input and discards the part before the chosen start time.
flags.duration: -t limits the output duration. It is a length of time, not an end time in the source.
flags.mapVideo: -map 0:v:0 selects the first video stream from input 0.
flags.mapAudio: -map '0:a?' selects audio from input 0 when it exists. The question mark makes that selection optional.
flags.encode: -c:v libx264 encodes pictures as H.264. -c:a aac encodes sound as AAC.
flags.pixels: -pix_fmt yuv420p chooses a widely supported way to store picture colour.
